chapter: Cass Carr, Crawley, Burnet and Cootie Williams
title: Cootie's band beats Duke Ellington in a battle at the Savoy
summary: Ellington arrived late and off form, and Cootie's loud, swinging band won the battle, which was rare for Ellington.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: What are you gonna do with a bunch of nuts? Eddie didn't think he did anything wrong. Boy, he didn't think he a thing wrong. But that's the way the band was. And I mean, there was always something going on. It was a joy to work with him, because... We played a battle of music against Duke Ellington at the Savoy Ballroom, and naturally, they billed "Cootie Williams, formerly of Duke Ellington's band [Cootie had a bit name in the Savoy] and Duke Ellington." So boy, here's the night of this battle of music.

Well, Duke didn't show up on time or something. Anyway, the band had to hit without Duke. And naturally, they were just messin' around with some numbers, you know, just playing, and they didn't sound good. Duke's band didn't sound up to par anyway, you know. So anyway, Cootie got on the stand and played his numbers, to get that first whack in. So man, the house was comin' down, boy. They
applauded and applauded. And next time we went up there he put Eddie Vinson on, singing his best numbers and so forth. While you got 'em down you keep 'em down, you know. So man, he was carryin' on.

So Duke did come in, but it was one of them things, if you don't start off right, you just don't get together. That was not Duke's night. And everybody in the place that night, they was applauding Cootie's band, and even the wives of the Ellington members were saying, "Yes, that's right. Duke got cut tonight." Well, they was as much for Cootie as anybody else, because all the wives knew Cootie from Duke's band. And they were saying, "Yes, Duke got cut tonight." Well, Duke wasn't in form that night, and the band wasn't in form -- believe me.

But Cootie did... Well, he outshouted them. They made more noise than Duke. We had a loud band. Of course, all the notes wasn't always right, but they could play loud. And they had a good beat. They had a hell of a beat. So I'll give Cootie that much. Yeah, I'll give him that much. It wasn't often that Duke lost a battle of music. Because Duke had so much stuff he could dig down there and bring out on you, you know, the average musician, you can't compete with him. But he didn't dig out nothing that night. Yeah, Cootie taken it away from him.
